title: bug: two worker seats provisioning their first worktrees at once race on .git/config, and one refuses with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED
description:
Found by architect-0fcb7226 while planning WT-19b (task-48aafb880ede4b22a3e26115c07f8470), 2026-11-02.

Cause: provision_worktree (sh) and Initialize-MoeWorktree (ps1) run `git -C W sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.moe/'` on a fresh W. If the repo's config lacks extensions.worktreeConfig, git first enables it in the COMMON .git/config and takes .git/config.lock to do so. When two seats provision at the same moment, one fails with `error: could not lock config file .git/config: File exists`. The wrapper then refuses that seat with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED (report_blocked, no CLI launch).

Repro (git 2.43, scratch dir outside the repo): create 20 fresh repos, add two `worktree add --no-checkout` worktrees to each, then run both `sparse-checkout set` calls in parallel. 2 of the 40 calls failed with that error.

Impact:
- This repo has extensions.worktreeConfig unset and no linked worktree, so the first concurrent worker claims after the switch can hit the race.
- WT-19b's parallel scenario would flake on it, about 10% of runs.
- Once the extension is set, it is per-worktree config and the race is gone.

Fix (wrapper lane files; twins):
- Before the sparse-checkout, when `git config --get extensions.worktreeConfig` is not `true`, run `git config extensions.worktreeConfig true`.
- Retry only the config-lock collision, a few times with a short backoff. If another seat already set it to true, that counts as success.
- Any other failure keeps today's MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED refusal.

Interim workaround for the switch checklist: run `git config extensions.worktreeConfig true` in the control checkout before relaunching seats.

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (plus, on a Windows seat, node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: provision_worktree and Initialize-MoeWorktree make sure extensions.worktreeConfig is true before W's first sparse-checkout. They retry only a config-lock collision, with a bounded number of attempts, and still refuse with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED on any other failure. bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.

A postflight-worktree.cjs case (sh and ps1 engines) deterministically forces the config-lock collision on the first write, and the seat still provisions W. A second case, with the extension already true, makes no config write.
Existing postflight-worktree.cjs and held-out worktree-landing cases pass unchanged.
The verification command exits 0; on a Windows seat, postflight-safe.mjs powershell passes.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh: add a helper `enable_worktree_config` and call it in provision_worktree. Read mem:gotcha-worktree-first-sparse-checkout-config-race first.

The call goes inside the existing `if [ "$added" = true ] || [ "$finish" = true ]` block, right before W's `sparse-checkout set` (moe-agent.sh ~:3119-3128 at HEAD 204cacb8). A reused W runs no sparse-checkout and no helper.

Helper semantics:
- `git -C "$MOE_TOP" config --get --type=bool extensions.worktreeConfig` already `true` → return 0 with no write. Never touch config otherwise.
- If the common config sets core.worktree, or core.bare is true, do NOT pre-set; return 0 so git's own sparse-checkout init runs as today. Reason: git's init_worktree_config relocates those two settings into config.worktree, and a plain config write would skip that. Say so in a comment.
- Otherwise, up to 5 attempts of `LC_ALL=C git -C "$MOE_TOP" config extensions.worktreeConfig true`. LC_ALL=C keeps the message matchable under any locale.
  - Success → 0.
  - Output containing `could not lock config file` → if a re-read now gives true (another seat won), return 0. Otherwise print `[info] MOE_WORKTREE_CONFIG_RETRY attempt=<n>/5: .git/config is locked by another git process` and sleep a short jittered backoff (about 0.2-0.6 s; fractional sleep works in GNU, macOS and Git Bash), then retry.
  - Any other output → return 1 at once with git's last line.
  - Attempts exhausted → return 1 naming the lock.

Error handling: a helper failure takes the SAME path as a failed sparse-checkout:
- the existing removal of an added W with no commits;
- then `worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED "…"` with the helper's detail.
There is no silent fallback to an unchecked sparse-checkout. Call the helper from the main shell, not inside $(...), so worktree_stop still exits the seat. The design comment above provision_worktree explains why. Twin comment: name the ps1 function.

Leave the gate arm (:5330) and the hooked scratch (:5171) alone. A worker's pre-flight provisioning always runs before them in the same repo and sets the extension; say so in the comment.

The gotcha: git returns 255 with `error: could not lock config file .git/config: File exists` (planner-verified). Match the message, not the exit code.

scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs: deterministic cases for both engines; the suite is shared by postflight.sh and postflight.ps1.

(a) Extend the PATH stub (stub() ~:120) in BOTH its sh `git` and its `git.ps1` with WT_GIT_CONFIG_LOCK=<count file>. When argv holds `config` and `extensions.worktreeConfig` without `--get`, and the file holds a number above 0:
- decrement it;
- print `error: could not lock config file .git/config: File exists` to stderr;
- exit 255.
Otherwise pass through to the real git. Make launch() (~:191) install the stub when WT_GIT_CONFIG_LOCK is set.

(b) Cases, all on a fresh repo() fixture whose config lacks the extension unless stated:
- `wt-config-lock` (count 1): `[worktree] created …` appears; exactly one MOE_WORKTREE_CONFIG_RETRY line; `git config --get extensions.worktreeConfig` == true; W's sparse patterns are `/*` and `!/.moe/`; no report_blocked; the CLI ran.
- `wt-config-lock-exhausted` (count 99): MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED via refused(); exactly 4 retry lines (5 attempts); the CLI did not run; no W directory or registration is left behind.
- `wt-config-other` (WT_GIT_FAIL=extensions.worktreeConfig): an immediate MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED with no retry line.
- `wt-config-preset`: the fixture sets extensions.worktreeConfig=true first. Provisioning succeeds; .git/config is byte-identical before and after; no retry line.

Assertions must fail if the helper is removed. Prove it in step 5's mutant run.

Do not edit the held-out worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}.

Adversarial self-review, then complete_task.

Mutant check, in a scratch copy of scripts/ outside the repo (mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-mutant-copy):
- drop the helper call → wt-config-lock and wt-config-lock-exhausted must fail with AssertionErrors;
- make every error retryable → wt-config-other must fail.
An unmutated control must pass. Record the results.

Checklist:
- Two seats at once: the retry, plus the re-read that treats another seat's write as success.
- The lock held by a human's git: bounded, then the old refusal.
- Localized git: LC_ALL=C on the write only.
- core.worktree or core.bare=true: today's path.
- A reused W: no write.
- PS 5.1 syntax, BOM kept, parity PASS.
- Shared mode untouched: the helper runs only in worktree provisioning.
- No new failure mode: every failure still lands on MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED with the existing cleanup.

Fix anything found, rerun step 4's command fresh, and submit that output.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Two worker seats provisioning their first task worktrees at once never refuse because of the shared .git/config lock. Before W's first sparse-checkout, provisioning makes sure extensions.worktreeConfig is true, retrying only a config-lock collision (bounded). git's sparse-checkout then writes only the per-worktree config.worktree. Any other failure still refuses with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED as today.
acceptanceCriteria:
DoD 1: provision_worktree and Initialize-MoeWorktree run the twin helper before W's first sparse-checkout.
- It makes no write when the extension is already true.
- It skips the pre-set (today's git path) when the common config sets core.worktree or core.bare=true.
- It makes at most 5 attempts, retrying only on `could not lock config file` and printing MOE_WORKTREE_CONFIG_RETRY.
- Any other failure gives MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED with the existing cleanup.
- parity-check passes.

DoD 2: postflight-worktree.cjs cases wt-config-lock (provisions after one forced collision) and wt-config-preset (no config write; .git/config byte-identical) pass on sh and ps1, together with wt-config-lock-exhausted and wt-config-other.
DoD 3: existing postflight-worktree.cjs cases and the held-out worktree-landing cases pass unchanged.
DoD 4: `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` exits 0, and `postflight-safe.mjs powershell` passes on Windows.
invariants: Shared mode is unchanged: the helper runs only in worktree provisioning.
A config value is written only when the extension is not already true, and only extensions.worktreeConfig, never anything else.
No path skips the refusal: an exhausted or non-lock failure refuses as today and leaves no added W behind.
The wrappers stay in string parity, and moe-agent.ps1 keeps its BOM.
compatibility: Repos whose common config sets core.worktree or core.bare=true keep git's own sparse-checkout upgrade path.
The gate arm and the hooked scratch sparse-checkouts are untouched; provisioning precedes them.
approvedScope: scripts/moe-agent.sh: enable_worktree_config plus its call in provision_worktree
scripts/moe-agent.ps1: Enable-MoeWorktreeConfig plus its call in Initialize-MoeWorktree
scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs: the WT_GIT_CONFIG_LOCK stub knob and 4 wt-config-* cases
reuse: The existing provision_worktree/Initialize-MoeWorktree failure and cleanup path.
postflight-worktree.cjs's stub(), launch(), repo() and refused() helpers.
sourceAssumptions: moe-agent.sh provision_worktree runs `sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.moe/'` only when added or finish (~:3119-3128 at 204cacb8). ps1 Initialize-MoeWorktree does the same at ~:2978. A reused W skips it.
git's first sparse-checkout in a linked worktree enables extensions.worktreeConfig in the common .git/config under config.lock. With two at once, one fails; reproduced 2/40 with git 2.43.

A lock collision prints `error: could not lock config file .git/config: File exists` with exit 255 (planner-verified with LC_ALL=C). git honors extensions.worktreeConfig at repositoryformatversion 0 (setup.c handle_extension_v0).
git's init_worktree_config moves core.worktree, and core.bare=true, into config.worktree, which a plain config write would skip. Hence the skip.
postflight-worktree.cjs stub() (~:120) has sh and ps1 forms with WT_GIT_VERSION/FAIL/SWAP knobs; launch() installs it only when one of those is set (~:191).
checkRefs: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Retrying `sparse-checkout set` itself on the lock error: rejected. The DoD requires the extension to be true BEFORE the first sparse-checkout, and a pre-set leaves sparse-checkout writing only config.worktree.
- Pre-setting it in fixtures or the switch checklist only: rejected as the fix, because it hides the race in tests. It stays as the governor's interim checklist step.
- Also guarding the gate arm and the hooked scratch: rejected (YAGNI). Worker pre-flight provisioning always runs first in the same repo.
- A real two-process race test in postflight-worktree.cjs: rejected, because the shared fake is single-seat. The deterministic stub covers it, and WT-19b's e2e runs real concurrent seats.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Provisioning's sparse-checkout runs only for an added or finished W.
- Its failure path already removes an added W with no commits before worktree_stop.
- The stub git has sh and ps1 twins, and launch() enables it per knob.
- parity-check compares MOE_WORKTREE_* code sets across the twins.
planningNotes.risks:
- PS 5.1 syntax and the BOM: use the Edit tool.
- Localized git messages: LC_ALL=C on the write.
- A helper inside $(...) cannot exit the seat: call it in the main shell.
- Backoff must be fractional sleep, available everywhere.
- postflight-safe runs 15-25 min: nohup plus a poll.
- The Windows leg needs node.exe from WSL (memories cited in step 4).
